question.worked_solution:
Notice that the dividend is missing the ${x}^{2}$-term. So, we write it using a zero coefficient, as follows:

$$
6{x}^{3}+0{x}^{2}-4x+5
$$

Using the method of polynomial division, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned} & \,\,\,\,\,3{x}^{2}-6x+10 \\  & 2x+4\,\enclose{longdiv}{\,\,6{x}^{3}+\phantom{1}0{x}^{2}-\phantom{1}4x+\phantom{1}5\,\,} \\  & \,\,\,\,\,{6{x}^{3}+12{x}^{2}}_{―} \\  & \,\,\,\,\,\,-\,12{x}^{2}-4x+5 \\  & \,\,\,\,\,\,{-\,12{x}^{2}-24x}_{―} \\  & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,20x+5 \\  & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,{20x+40}_{―} \\  & \,\,\,\,\,\,-\,35\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the missing expressions are

$\,$ $3{x}^{2}-6x+10\,$ and $\,20x+5.$
